Hi Samantha  thanks, and thanks Marissa for looping us in. A few notes / assumptions so the workbook maps to expected cost/latency: 

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Average request: 80 tokens in, ~120 tokens out.
- Peak user-facing QPS: 150 (10-minute burst windows).
- P95 latency target: 200ms per request for token generation portion.

Recommendation (starter config):
- Serving pool: start with 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (model-dependent) dedicated for low-latency serving. Configure per-GPU concurrent slots so that per-slot throughput keeps p95 < 200ms. For many open models, that's roughly 68 concurrent request slots per GPU depending on prompt length and model.
- Worker pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for embeddings/reranks (can be batch-optimized / quantized).
- Autoscaling: scale serving pool by whole-GPU increments with a target CPU/GPU utilization threshold (e.g., scale up when queue depth > 20 and average GPU util > 65%). Configure a fast scale-up (burst) policy to add capacity within 60120s for sustained spikes.
- Queueing/concurrency: front-door request queue with per-customer quota tokens, and a soft concurrency limit per-slot to prevent head-of-line blocking. Suggested per-request queue timeout 10s and a max queue depth organized by priority (interactive vs. batch).
- Concurrency limits: per-connection limit (e.g., 4 streams) plus per-slot concurrency (68). This combination prevents overloads while maximizing utilization.
- Routing/fallbacks: route to cheaper quantized model variants under heavy load; keep a warm pool of smaller models for critical paths.

What we need from you to firm numbers:
- A 24-72h sample of request logs with tokens/request and timestamps (sample attached earlier helps).
- Confirmation of allowed burst tolerance (how much added latency or throttling is acceptable during bursts).

I'll upload a filled example sheet to the Drive link Marissa shared and include the scaling formulas so you can tweak assumptions. Happy to walk through the workbook on Friday.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
